The New Health Options Act of 2025 (H.R. 1776) is a critical step toward dismantling Obamacare’s rigid frameworks that trapped families in unaffordable plans. By creating a reinsurance program for off-exchange plans, it allows insurers to bypass the single risk pool mandate—a key driver of premium spikes under prior administrations. 

The bill’s $6 billion annual cap ensures fiscal responsibility while letting insurers adjust age-based pricing beyond the 3:1 ratio, reflecting real actuarial risk. This aligns with efforts to break bureaucratic strangleholds on healthcare, though the real test will be whether it forces hospitals and insurers to compete on price transparency. 

Families deserve options beyond one-size-fits-all mandates—this bill starts that process.

The Southern Coalfields water crisis exposes a systemic failure of accountability—Wyoming County residents waited 5+ years while bureaucrats shuffled permits between bankrupt coal companies (Pinnacle/Bluestone/Alpha) and agencies like WVDEP issued hollow assurances. Moore’s amendment (H.R.5108 Sec.118) finally directs $18M to water infrastructure, but let’s be clear: this funding should’ve been prioritized DECADES ago under existing Clean Water Act mandates.

The fact that Congress is just now acting—after independent testing proved sulfate-reducing bacteria, hydrogen sulfide, and heavy metals poisoning entire watersheds—shows how D.C. defaults to crisis management over prevention. Audit every dollar to ensure it bypasses bloated state admin and flows DIRECTLY to filtration systems + pipeline repairs.

No more subsidizing corporate negligence—make permit holders fund remediation or lose mining rights.
